what_this_is: One labelled Terminal-Bench 2.1 arm: SINGLE pass, DOUBLED agent timeout, on the 8x DP8 tier. It exists to separate budget-bound failures from fidelity-bound failures. It is NOT leaderboard-comparable because the agent timeout is non-stock, and it does NOT revise the published 31/89 (single pass, stock clock) or 44/89 (best-of-2, stock clock) numbers.

comparison_ladder.note: The clean one-variable pair is 31 -> 56, both single pass. The +25 comes from doubled clock AND the 8x tier together; both act through the SAME channel (tokens available before the deadline) and neither is a fidelity channel, so the pair bounds budget-bound failure without being a scaling claim.

quantization_suspect.verdict: WITHDRAWN. All seven tasks previously labelled quantization-suspect resolve ON THE QUANTIZED MODEL once the clock is doubled. BF16 passing them at stock clock was therefore not evidence of a fidelity deficit; those failures were budget-bound. Zero tasks in the suite remain attributable to quantization.

capability.verdict: The only genuine capability failure in the suite; unchanged by clock or tier.

harness_void.verdict: Both RuntimeErrors in this arm are exactly these two tasks. Nested-virtualisation qemu is unavailable on the Jarvis VM, so they are structurally unattemptable here, not failures.

regressions_vs_best_of_2.explanation: This arm is SINGLE pass; 44/89 was BEST-OF-2. Five tasks that succeeded on one of two stock-clock attempts failed on this single attempt. That is ordinary best-of-1 vs best-of-2 variance, reported rather than netted out: the arm gained 17 and lost 5 for +12 net against 44.

honest_limits: Non-stock timeout: never quote 56/89 as a Terminal-Bench score.
Tier and timeout co-varied; no per-variable split is claimed.
Single pass, so its own unresolved set carries best-of-1 variance.
The two qemu tasks are environment-void here and would need a nested-virt host to attempt.
